exposure: CP characteristics (type, topography, distribution, Gross Motor Function Classification System [GMFCS] level)
outcome: time lag from suspicion to diagnosis
cohort: The study included 99 preterm infants born <29 weeks gestation and/or with birthweight <1000g who were diagnosed with cerebral palsy and followed in Calgary's Neonatal Follow-up Clinic between January 2005 and December 2014.
finding: CP diagnosis timing was affected by the Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) level, motor type (mixed vs. spastic only), and motor distribution (upper and lower extremities involvement), with higher GMFCS levels, mixed type, and upper/lower extremity involvement associated with earlier diagnosis.
followup_time: Up to and beyond 19 months corrected age (median age at diagnosis was 19 months corrected age).
